title: Iqbal Hussain v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Sunita Agarwal and Vivek Varma, JJ.
disposition: Writ dismissed; petitioner relegated to Supply Code 6.8(b).
headnote: A writ petition challenging assessment of electricity charges on a temporary connection is not maintainable. The consumer must take that grievance to the competent authority under clause 6.8(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.
facts: Iqbal Hussain filed a writ petition in the High Court of Judicature at Allahabad challenging assessment of electricity charges on a temporary connection granted to him for 90 days. On 7 July 2020 the matter was adjourned because the petition had been filed without serving respondent no. 3. On 13 July 2020 the Court granted that respondent a week to seek instructions and directed that no coercive measure be taken against the petitioner until the next listing.

holding_units.topic: assessment of electricity dues — alternate remedy
holding_units.holding: Where the consumer is aggrieved by assessment of electricity charges, including charges on a temporary connection granted for 90 days, the appropriate remedy is to approach the competent authority under clause 6.8(b) of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the writ petition is dismissed.

principle_tags.application: Applied to dismiss a writ challenging assessment of charges on a 90-day temporary connection; clause 6.8(b) of the Supply Code is the competent forum.

not_decided.point: Correctness of the assessment of electricity charges on the petitioner's 90-day temporary connection
not_decided.note: The Court did not examine the assessment on merits and relegated the petitioner to clause 6.8(b).
